knowledge_graph.title: Property tax
knowledge_graph.description: A property tax is an ad valorem tax on the value of a property. The tax is levied by the governing authority of the jurisdiction in which the property is located. This can be a national government, a federated state, a county or other geographical region, or a municipality.

related_questions.question: What is the meaning of real estate tax?
related_questions.snippet: What Are Real Estate Taxes? Real estate taxes are the same as real property taxes. They are levied on most properties in America and paid to state and local governments. The funds generated from real estate taxes (or real property taxes) are typically used to help pay for local and state services.

related_questions.question: Are real estate taxes the same as state taxes?
related_questions.snippet: Taxpayers in all 50 states and the District of Columbia pay property taxes, but the tax on real property is primarily levied by local governments (cities, counties, and school districts) rather than state governments. With a few exceptions, states typically levy taxes on personal property.

related_questions.question: Is real estate tax included in a mortgage?
related_questions.snippet: Most likely, your property taxes will be included in your monthly mortgage payments. While this may make your payments larger, it will allow you to avoid paying a thousand dollars (or more) in one sitting. And with your lender's help, you can ensure your property tax payments are made in full and on time.
